obligations.note: The access matrix (rbac.py) and access-policy.json are unchanged; the new route reuses the existing privileged action 'manage_payees' which is already in the approved policy. The CI control test test_matrix_equals_approved_policy passed.
The auditor role in the access policy has no state-changing actions; this change does not modify rbac.py or the policy. The CI test test_auditor_is_read_only passed.
The segregation-of-duties entry (it_admin must_not approve/release payments) is unchanged; the new route uses 'manage_payees', not a credit or payment-release action. CI test passed.

The new route 'POST /payees/{id}/reopen' has action 'manage_payees', which is listed as privileged in access-policy.json, yet is defined with mfa=False. The CI test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa failed, flagging this route. The cited exception EXC-0210 expired on 2026-09-03, well before the 2026-10-12 review time, so it cannot justify the deviation.

The session timeout logic in session.py is unchanged; the new route goes through the same _authenticate path that enforces privileged idle timeout. The CI test test_privileged_idle_timeout_within_policy passed.
The new SQL (UPDATE payees SET status='open', closed_at=NULL WHERE id=?) touches only non-NPI columns; NPI fields remain sealed via the vault. The CI encryption control test passed.
No integration or transport code is modified; the CI integrations TLS test passed.
The new service method logs only 'reopen_payee' with actor, action, and payee_id via the audit path; no NPI values are written to application logs. The CI logging test passed.
The new state-changing operation reopen_payee calls self._audit(actor, 'reopen_payee', f'payee:{payee_id}'), recording actor, action, target, and time. The CI sampled audit test passed.
audit.py is not modified; the hash-chaining and retention logic remain intact. The CI test test_chain_and_retention passed and the modelcheck evidence in ACR-0402 covers unchanged code.

Reopening a payee sets status='open' and closed_at=NULL, which simply removes it from the closed-payee purge pipeline; it does not bypass legal-hold checks or alter the retention schedule. The CI retention test passed.
No new outbound integrations are added; the CI integrations inventory test passed.
The new SQL statement uses a fixed string with a parameterised placeholder (? for payee_id); no string interpolation from data. The CI SQL parameterisation test passed.
No payment creation or approval logic is modified; the maker-checker mechanism in payments.py is untouched. The CI maker-checker test passed.
The dual-control threshold and approval logic in payments.py and policy.py are unchanged; the CI dual-control test passed and the proof record in ACR-0401 covers unchanged code.
No changes to the release logic in payments.py or store.py's find_release/add_release; the CI idempotency test passed and the ponens trace in ACR-0403 covers unchanged code.
Ticket CHG-25756 is approved by change_manager grace.kim; its components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.service, payments.store) cover all four files modified by the change.
A code_review approval from sofia.santos (change_approver for payments, not the author mara.costa) is on record for the head commit.
The single commit in the change is f280478, and both approvals reference that exact SHA; there are no later commits that could void them.

The CI run on the final commit (f280478) reports 1 failure: test_privileged_routes_require_mfa. The full test suite did not pass, violating the requirement that the app's full suite pass on the final commit.

The change touches security-sensitive components (payments.http, payments.routes, payments.store); a security_review approval from ines.halvorsen (security_reviewer, not the author) is recorded for the head commit.
No file under the protected paths (controls/*, ci/*, tests/controls/*) is modified; the change is confined to apps/baseline-payments/payments/.
The ticket type is 'standard', not 'emergency'; no post-implementation review is required.

The only exception cited (EXC-0210, MFA-1, payments.routes) expired on 2026-09-03, which is before the 2026-10-12 review time. Per the change policy, expired exceptions do not count, so the MFA-1 deviation is unexcused.

ACR-0404 (MFA-1 evidence) covers apps/baseline-payments/payments/routes.py, which is behaviourally changed by adding a new route. The evidence lapses and no replacement passing evidence exists because the CI MFA-1 test fails.

summary: The change adds a POST /payees/{id}/reopen route whose action 'manage_payees' is classified as privileged in the access policy, yet the route is declared with mfa=False, directly violating MFA-1. The CI test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails, confirming the violation. The only exception that could excuse this (EXC-0210) expired on 2026-09-03, well before the 2026-10-12 review date, and therefore cannot justify the deviation. Additionally, CHG-4 is violated because the full test suite does not pass on the final commit, and LAP-1 is violated because the MFA-1 evidence in ACR-0404 lapses due to the behavioural change to routes.py with no replacement evidence. The change must be rejected.
